phrases.say: Nifty fell four hundred and fifty points today.
From the day's high, it lost over six hundred.
Here are the five reasons.
Reason one. Profit booking.
Nifty had rallied about ten percent this month,
phrases.cap: Nifty was up about *10%* this month

phrases.say: and touched twenty five thousand nine hundred ninety two, just below twenty six thousand.
Traders sold near that wall.
Reason two. Banks.
Bank Nifty fell over three percent, right after a record high.
H D F C Bank alone fell three point three percent.
Reason three. Tata Steel crashed eight percent.
It agreed to buy twenty six percent of A P L Apollo Tubes for fifteen thousand five hundred crore rupees,
phrases.cap: Buying *26.6%* of APL Apollo for *₹15,510 Cr*

phrases.say: plus an open offer for twenty six percent more.
phrases.cap: plus an open offer for *26%* more

phrases.say: Investors did not like the bill.
Reason four. America.
The Fed's minutes sounded tougher on inflation.
Traders now see a ninety three percent chance of a December rate hike.
Higher US rates can pull foreign money out of India.
Reason five. The rupee.
It closed at ninety two point six seven on Friday, and slipped toward ninety three.
A weak rupee makes foreign investors nervous.
So, is this a crash?
Nifty closed at twenty five thousand three hundred fifty.
That's still only about four percent below its record high.
One red day is not a crash.
